chapter: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
title: Jamming for pleasure and Piney Brown, patron saint of Kansas City musicians
summary: Musicians had no money, but Kansas City's Piney Brown, a numbers man, looked after Barefield and Ben Webster, paying rent and getting their horns out of pawn.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: So it wasn't all about money in those days?
No, we never had any money.
Just enough so you had something to eat and a place to stay?

Right. And like in Kansas City, there was a guy in Kansas City named Piney Brown who was a patron saint of musicians. And he was like a father to Ben Webster and I everytime we wanted to go to work. We used to go to work to get our horns out of the pawnshop, and we'd go to work. And Piney took care of us, paid our rent and took us out with girls and everything. He was in the number business so we'd go out there sometimes to stay three or four days, drinking and having a ball and playing. And if Piney ran out of money he'd go to the place and come back with $200, $300.00 more. You know, just keep the thing going.
